newsitem.title: USA: US crudes dive lower on paper sell-off, grades off.
newsitem.headline: US crudes dive lower on paper sell-off, grades off.

text.p: Technical selling on the NYMEX futures market depressed cash outright crudes in the U.S. on Friday, while grade differentials remained weaker in modestly traded afternoon activity.

At 1421 EDT (1800 GMT), July futures were 59 cents lower at $19.07 a barrel. Cash benchmark July West Texas Intermediate/Cushing remained firmly above the futures on the strength in Exchange for Physicals, which were last sold at +20 cents, putting cash at $19.20-30 a barrel.

For the grades, Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James was pegged at 25-20 cents under July cash WTI, five cents weaker than late Thursday. Latest deals for LLS were confirmed at 20 and 22 cts discounts, traders said.

Sour barrels failed to move from morning levels which increased their discounts to the benchmark by some 10-20 cents. Eugene Island was pegged around a $1.90 discount to the benchmark, with West Texas Sour/Midland at WTI/Cushing -$1.75.
Cash players said LLS was deflated by arbitrage economics for bringing over North Sea Brent, and West African Bonny Light offerings in the Gulf.

Outside factors in the market were quiet, with most of the outright price pressure generated from charts showing technical weakness. This week's inventory data showing sizable crude builds, and sentiment more than enough crude is available has awakened bears in the market.
